messages:
elaine: Hey team — docs PR #4324 is blocked. I wrote the migration notes for config overrides but I need confirmation on the binding/precedence order before we ship. Can someone from runtime confirm?

amjad: which specific override are you worried about? route vs model vs global?

elaine: Yeah, and also how 'null' or omitted keys behave during merge. The stanza in the PR says: 'route config overrides model defaults, which override global defaults' but runtime behavior might be more nuanced (can a route explicitly set null to inherit?).

liam: quick ping — I hit this too in a separate migration guide. Runtime used to treat absent keys as inherit, but explicit `null` was a signal to unset in older versions.

runtime-engineer: short answer: precedence is route > deployment > model > global. Longer: when evaluating a config key we first look for an explicit value on the route, then on the deployment binding, then model-level defaults, then global defaults. Important nuance: explicit `null` is considered a value that overrides lower levels and causes the effective config to be unset.

elaine: Hmm ok. So explicit `null` removes the key even if a model default exists? That matches what liam said. Can you paste a minimal example we can put into the docs?

runtime-engineer: sure — example to include in docs:```yamlroute_config:  # route-level
  max_tokens: null  # explicit unset -> inherits nothing from model
deployment_config:  # deployment-level
  max_tokens: 1024
model_defaults:
  max_tokens: 2048
global_defaults:
  max_tokens: 4096
# Effective max_tokens for the route above -> null/unset (route wins)```

selina: so callers should expect that if a route unsets something, the runtime treats it as absent and some downstream logic (batching/caching) may fall back to safe defaults. We should document that explicit unsets can affect batching heuristics.

runtime-engineer: yes — add a short note: "Explicit null/unset at a higher precedence prevents lower precedence values from applying; some runtime subsystems will substitute hardcoded safe defaults when a value is unset." That's what the runtime does to avoid surprising NPEs.

elaine: ok adding: "Precedence order: route > deployment > model > global. Explicit null at any level counts as an explicit override that prevents lower levels from applying. When a required field becomes unset, runtime subsystems may use internal safe defaults — see batching and caching notes." Does that sound accurate?

runtime-engineer: accurate. Also call out the migration caveat: older runtime (<v1.8) treated explicit null as inherit in some fields — we should warn users to check their runtime version.

liam: thanks — can we include a tiny migration checklist? e.g., grep for `max_tokens:` + `null` and decide whether to set explicit values before upgrade.

elaine: will add a 1-line checklist and link to the runtime changelog. One last question: merge timing — docs CI preview needs this before we merge because the examples show behavior. Is a runtime engineer review + LGTM enough or do we need a formal sign-off from product?

runtime-engineer: LGTM from runtime + a quick QA sanity check on staging is sufficient for this doc change. If it touches SLAs or pricing behavior, loop in product. This one is safe.

elaine: great. I'll update the PR with the YAML example and the version caveat, run the docs preview, and request `runtime-engineer` approval.

selina: :thumbsup:

docs-bot: Preview build started for branch docs/pr-4324 — link: https://docs-preview.internal/reports/4324

elaine: thanks — will wait for preview link then merge once runtime-engineer approves and CI passes.
